claims.text: Role in rabies: after exposure: clean and debride wounds, then give the vaccine and rabies immune globulin;
claims.quote: After exposure to an animal who has or is suspected of having rabies, thoroughly clean and debride any wounds, then give the rabies vaccine and rabies immune globulin.

claims.text: RIG 20 IU/kg infiltrated around the wound (some IM if the volume is too much for distal sites, eg, fingers, nose);
claims.quote: For postexposure prophylaxis, rabies immune globulin 20 IU/kg is infiltrated around the wound for passive immunization; if injection volume is too much for distal areas (eg, fingers, nose), some rabies immune globulin may be given IM

claims.text: HDCV: four 1-mL IM doses (deltoid preferred) from day 0, in a limb other than the RIG one, then days 3, 7 and 14; immunosuppressed: a fifth dose on day 28;
claims.quote: HDCV is given in a series of four 1-mL IM injections (deltoid area is preferred), beginning on the day of exposure (day 0), in a limb other than the one used for rabies immune globulin. Subsequent injections occur on days 3, 7, and 14; immunosuppressed patients receive a fifth dose on day 28.

claims.text: previously vaccinated: 1-mL IM vaccine on days 0 and 3, no RIG;
claims.quote: Postexposure prophylaxis for a person previously vaccinated against rabies includes 1-mL IM injections of rabies vaccine on days 0 and 3 but no rabies immune globulin.

claims.text: once clinical rabies develops, vaccine + RIG may cause faster deterioration.
claims.quote: Administering rabies vaccine and immune globulin after clinical rabies develops may cause more rapid deterioration.

claims.text: Rabies immune globulin (HyperRAB) label: use only w the vaccine series, never alone;
claims.quote: Use HYPERRAB in combination with rabies vaccine series to be effective. Do not use HYPERRAB alone for prevention.

claims.text: give at the first vaccine dose (day 0), no later than day 7;
claims.quote: Administer HYPERRAB at the time of the first vaccine dose (day 0), but no later than day 7.

claims.text: infiltrate the full dose around the wound if feasible (dilute w D5W, ⍉ NS, if more volume is needed); inject the rest IM (deltoid or lateral thigh) away from the vaccine site;
claims.quote: Infiltrate the full dose of HYPERRAB in the area around the wound, if anatomically feasible. Dilute HYPERRAB with an equal volume of dextrose, 5% (D5W), if additional volume is needed to infiltrate the entire wound. Do not dilute with normal saline. Inject the remainder, if any, of the HYPERRAB dose intramuscularly into the deltoid muscle of the upper arm or into the lateral thigh muscle, and distant from the site of vaccine administration.

claims.text: ⍉ same syringe, needle or site as the vaccine;
claims.quote: Do not administer HYPERRAB in the same syringe or needle or in the same anatomic site as vaccine.

claims.text: ⍉ repeat doses once the vaccine is started (blunts active immunity);
claims.quote: Do not administer repeated doses of HYPERRAB once vaccine treatment has been initiated as this could prevent the full expression of active immunity expected from the rabies vaccine.

claims.text: defer live vaccines for 4 months after.
claims.quote: Defer immunization with live vaccines for 4 months after HYPERRAB administration.

claims.text: Severe hypersensitivity possible (↑ risk w prior systemic rxns to human Ig): keep epinephrine available.
claims.quote: Severe hypersensitivity reactions may occur with HYPERRAB. Patients with a history of prior systemic allergic reactions to human immunoglobulin preparations are at a greater risk of developing severe hypersensitivity and anaphylactic reactions. Have epinephrine available for treatment of acute allergic symptoms, should they occur.

claims.text: Rabies vaccine (Imovax) label: adults and older children: IM into the deltoid;
claims.quote: For adults and older children, the vaccine should be injected into the deltoid muscle.
Do not administer in the gluteal area
